segments.title: HMS Azalea, HMS Zinnia, and the Flower class
segments.summary: A photograph of HMS Azalea, the class nameship, introduces HMS Zinnia, an early Flower-class corvette-sloop whose career spanned both world wars.
segments.body: The opening image shows HMS Azalea, the class nameship, while the discussion turns to HMS Zinnia. Zinnia belonged to the early Flower class, described here as a corvette-sloop. Her career reached across both world wars.

evidence.note: The transcript identifies the image as Azalea, then introduces Zinnia as an early Flower-class corvette-sloop serving through both world wars.

segments.title: From HMS Zinnia to Barbara and Breidel
segments.summary: Royal Navy service ended with a 1920 sale to Belgium. Germany captured the ship in 1940 and renamed her Barbara before she returned to Belgian service as Breidel in 1945.
segments.body: Zinnia remained in Royal Navy service until 1920, when Belgium bought her. Germany captured the ship in 1940 and operated her as Barbara. She surrendered to the Allies in 1945, then returned to Belgian service under the name Breidel. Her career ended with scrapping in 1952. The same hull therefore passed through British, Belgian, and German service during a career that crossed both world wars.

evidence.note: The transcript follows Zinnia from Royal Navy service and sale to Belgium through German capture, postwar return, Belgian renaming, and scrapping.

segments.title: Zinnia, U-44, and the Begonia rescue
segments.summary: On 28 March 1916, Zinnia fired two shots at U-44 off Fastnet Rock. After the submarine torpedoed Begonia the next day, Zinnia and Snowdrop towed the damaged sloop to Queenstown.
segments.body: On 28 March 1916, Zinnia sighted the German submarine U-44 off Fastnet Rock and opened fire. Both shells fell short, and U-44 escaped by diving. The next day, the submarine torpedoed the sloop Begonia, but Begonia remained afloat. Zinnia and Snowdrop were ordered to assist and towed the damaged vessel into Queenstown. Within two days, Zinnia had attempted to engage a submarine and helped save another Flower-class sloop, an example of the varied work assigned to these small ships.

evidence.note: The transcript describes Zinnia's sighting and shots at U-44, the later torpedoing of Begonia, and the tow to Queenstown with Snowdrop.
